Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Burlington VT
645 AM EDT Thu Sep 3 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
As of 221 AM EDT Thursday...

No significant changes have been made to the forecast.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 221 AM EDT Thursday...

1. After more widespread precipitation overnight and early this 
morning, showers will become more scattered. Chances for afternoon 
showers will continue throughout the week, before drier conditions 
return towards Sunday.   

2. Several rounds of showers expected next week but no 
significant weather expected.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 221 AM EDT Thursday...

KEY MESSAGE 1: 

Widespread precipitation continues to push through the region this 
hour, although rainfall amounts are not nearly impressive as they 
were earlier in the night when KMSS measured over 3 inches of 
rainfall within a fairly short window. Showers will trend more 
scattered as the day progresses, with the best chances for 
additional rainfall across eastern Vermont and the northern Green 
Mountains although amounts will generally be light. Gusty southerly 
winds continue across the region this hour, particularly on Lake 
Champlain, but will diminish towards daybreak and become more 
northwesterly by this afternoon. Additional chances for diurnally 
driven showers will continue through the rest of the week, with the 
greatest chances across the high terrain while the broader valleys 
remain on the drier side. High pressure looks to build in
towards Sunday, bringing some drier weather. Temperatures will 
be on the cooler side as we remain under the influence of an 
upper low, with high temperatures generally in the upper 60s to 
mid 70s by this weekend.

KEY MESSAGE 2: Deep layer ridging will make a brief appearance on 
Monday bringing sunshine, light winds and seasonal temperatures to 
the North Country and northern New York. This period of dry weather 
will be short-lived as a shortwave trough in the northwesterly flow 
aloft flattens the longwave ridge and drives a cold front through 
the region Monday night into Tuesday morning. This should spark a 
few showers but no thunderstorms or impactful weather are expected 
with this system as we will seriously lack deep moisture. 
Thereafter, a series of low amplitude shortwaves are expected to 
move across the region through the second half of the work week. 
Period of light showers seem plausible through much of the week with 
ample period of dry weather between rounds of showers. However, if 
you are looking for an extended period of dry weather, next week 
does not look favorable for that at this time.

&&

.AVIATION /12Z THURSDAY THROUGH MONDAY/...
Through 12Z Friday...Widely variable conditions are currently
being observed with VFR ceilings in the Champlain Valley with
MVFR to IFR ceilings elsewhere. We will continue to see these
lower ceilings through 14Z with quick improvement expected this
morning. South to southwest winds ranging from 10 to 20 knots
will be common this morning with winds veering toward the WNW
this afternoon and weakening throughout the day. Rain chances
are looking rather lackluster and have removed all PROB30 groups
as the chances any terminal sees a shower today remain very low.
Depending on how quickly clouds move out of the region this
evening, we could see a favorable night for widespread fog
across the region.

Outlook...

Friday: VFR. Chance SHRA.
Friday Night: Mainly VFR, with local IFR possible. Chance SHRA.
Saturday: Mainly MVFR, with local IFR possible. Chance SHRA.
Saturday Night: Mainly VFR, with local MVFR possible. NO SIG WX.
Sunday: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Sunday Night: VFR. NO SIG WX.
